blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from Jared's known local notes (researched November 1, 2026). Listing-stated figures are labelled; unconfirmed items say so. No live listing feed or board statistics are attached to this page yet.

Where condo stock concentrates: there is no apartment-condo shelf. The community's strata stock is three bare-land strata / detached cottage communities on Columbia Valley Road; the rest of the housing is lake cottages and cabins — many originally seasonal, progressively converted to year-round homes — plus newer custom lake homes along the south-shore strip, predominantly freehold.
This guide covers Lindell Beach's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask.
Condo buildings in Lindell Beach

Lindell Beach is not inside the City of Chilliwack, despite "Chilliwack, BC" mailing addresses. It is an unincorporated community at the south end of Cultus Lake in Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area H; permits, zoning and services run through the FVRD and, for the lake's park lands, the Cultus Lake Park Board framework — not Chilliwack City Hall. It is a CADREB board sub-area under the MLS area Cultus Lake.
Streets, schools and transit near Lindell Beach condos

items.t: Lindell Beach sits at the south end of Cultus Lake; Columbia Valley Road is the single access road, running north past the community to Chilliwack and the Highway 1 Vedder Road interchange, and south toward Columbia Valley and the U.S. border. The community's named addresses line Columbia Valley Road: Lindell Beach Holiday Resort at 1920, The Cottages at Cultus Lake at 1777, Aquadel Crossing at 1885, and Creekside Mills in the same south-lake area.

Where condo stock concentrates: there is no apartment-condo shelf. The community's strata stock is three bare-land strata / detached cottage communities on Columbia Valley Road; the rest of the housing is lake cottages and cabins — many originally seasonal, progressively converted to year-round homes — plus newer custom lake homes along the south-shore strip, predominantly freehold.

Services: FVRD service areas, not city utilities — the Cultus Lake Integrated Water Supply and Distribution system and the South Cultus Lake Sewage Treatment system, with parcel taxes on participating properties. South-shore billing: FVRD Area H rates list Water – Cultus Lake (485) and Sewer – Cultus Lake South (448) as "No Utility Billing / Property Taxes: Yes" (tax-funded), while Sewer – Cultus Lake North (441) carries a $1,369.00 flat rate for 2026 plus taxes. Area H also has two fire services (Cultus Lake 213 and Columbia Valley 215) and no FVRD garbage/recycling service.

Schools are School District 33 (Chilliwack): Cultus Lake Community School, 71 Sunnyside Blvd in Cultus Lake Park, is the lake's elementary school; SD33 AP 611 groups the Columbia Valley/Cultus Lake area as Cultus Lake Elementary → Mount Slesse Middle → G.W. Graham Secondary. Catchments are address-based — confirm a specific address in SD33's locator.

Transit and shopping: no public transit serves Lindell Beach — the nearest BC Transit service is in Chilliwack, and Route 56 reaches only the north-end Marina, summer only. There is no commercial centre in Lindell Beach; daily shopping is in Sardis/Garrison Crossing (Chilliwack), north on Columbia Valley Road.
Population context: Statistics Canada counted 2,459 people in all of FVRD Electoral Area H in 2021 (+33.1% from 1,847 in 2016); no Lindell Beach-only figure is published.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Lindell Beach

items.t: Governing plan and zoning (FVRD, not Chilliwack): One zone is confirmed from a primary/developer source: PRD-1, Private Resort Residential Development (Creekside Mills). Zone and minimum parcel size for the older beach-strip lots: check per address in Bylaw 1638 / the FVRD webmap. No Chilliwack bylaw number governs this area, and none is borrowed here.

Short-term rentals: the FVRD Board specifically enabled Electoral Area H (Lindell Beach) to proactively address short-term vacation rentals and RV use for accommodation. The mechanism is zoning: Bylaw 1638 excludes "Temporary Tourist Accommodation" from Residential use except where a zone expressly permits it. Provincially, hosts have needed a registration number since May 1, 2025; electoral areas are exempt from the provincial principal-residence rule unless the board opts in. A seller's Airbnb history is not proof a buyer can continue it.

Flood / alluvial-fan layer: FVRD Floodplain Management Bylaw No. 1669, 2022 applies region-wide except municipalities and Park lands — so it applies here — and requires alluvial-fan development to meet the flood construction level/setback set by a site-specific geohazard assessment by a Professional Engineer/Geoscientist. The FVRD's Frosst Creek works (two debris basins and two dikes, south and north sides of the creek, partly on private property) protect the community on the Frosst Creek alluvial fan at the lake's south end.

Rural taxes (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11): Lindell Beach properties pay rural (provincial) property taxes plus FVRD service parcel taxes. Rural taxes are due and payable July 2, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid on July 2 and a further 5% penalty on amounts unpaid on October 31. The South Cultus Lake sewer parcel tax (service area established by Bylaw No. 1416, 2017; parcel tax by Bylaw No. 1497, 2018; Amendment Bylaw No. 1779, 2025) is the annual requisition divided equally among parcels on the roll, and south-shore water/sewer are tax-funded with no separate utility bill.

Manufactured-home parks (the Holiday Resort / park discussion): park tenancies run on park rules and the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act framework, not strata bylaws; annual pad-rent increases are capped at inflation plus a proportional amount for specified cost increases — 2.3% + proportional for 2026 and 2.2% + proportional for 2027. A park's age rule must be verified from the park itself in writing — a listing adjective is not verification (the Cultus Lake Village conflict in is the standing example).

blocks.text: Good to know about Lindell Beach condos

items.t: The north side of the lake got its sewage upgrade first (2025). The FVRD's North Cultus wastewater plant was commissioned in April 2025 (construction July 2023, substantial completion December 2024) under the Liquid Waste Management Plan (approved 2019), producing Class A effluent with phosphorus removal via rapid infiltration basins — while the south shore (Lindell Beach) remains on the South Cultus Lake Sewage Treatment service, funded by its equal-share parcel tax (Bylaw 1497, as amended by 1779, 2025).

Lindell Beach is named in its own OCP. OCP Bylaw No. 1115, 2011 is titled "Columbia Valley, Lindell Beach and Chilliwack River Valley" — the community is small, but it is a named planning community of Electoral Area H, not a Chilliwack neighbourhood that drifted south.

The Holiday Resort's tenure was settled in court, not in a brochure. The leading public record for Lindell Beach's biggest complex is a 2009 BC Court of Appeal decision (2009 BCCA 5) describing leased pads and owner-placed trailers — a reminder that resort "ownership" at the lake can mean owning a trailer and renting the ground under it.

Area H is growing fast — on paper, at least (2021 Census). Electoral Area H grew 33.1% between 2016 and 2021 (1,847 → 2,459 people), the context behind the new strata cottage communities at the lake's south end.

"Chilliwack" on the envelope, FVRD at the counter. Building permits, zoning enforcement and services for a Lindell Beach address all run through the FVRD; Chilliwack City Hall has no jurisdiction, even though the mailing address, the school district (SD33) and the MLS board (CADREB) all say Chilliwack.

South-shore services carry no utility bill — the north shore's does. The FVRD's Area H 2026 rates show Water – Cultus Lake and Sewer – Cultus Lake South as tax-funded ("No Utility Billing"), while Sewer – Cultus Lake North carries a $1,369.00 flat rate for 2026 plus taxes — two sides of the same lake on two different billing models. Services: FVRD service-area systems, not city utilities — the Cultus Lake Integrated Water Supply and Distribution system and the South Cultus Lake Sewage Treatment system, with parcel taxes on participating properties. Recreation anchor: the community is built around its residents' beach and docks on Cultus Lake's south shore; Cultus Lake Park's Main Beach, trails and the Waterpark/Adventure Park area are a short drive north, and BC Parks' Delta Grove Campground sits at the southeast end, year-round.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Lindell Beach

items.t: Regional plan: the plan is OCP Bylaw No. 1115, 2011 for Electoral Areas E and H — the FVRD titles it "Columbia Valley, Lindell Beach and Chilliwack River Valley," so Lindell Beach is covered by name — as amended by Bylaw No. 1533, 2019.

Regional zoning: outside the Park, Consolidated Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021 (approved Oct. 27, 2022, consolidating nine earlier bylaws); Bylaw No. 1375, 2016 applies only inside Cultus Lake Park and does not govern Lindell Beach. Zone and minimum parcel size for the older beach-strip lots: check per address in Bylaw 1638 / the FVRD webmap.

Short-term rentals: control is via zoning — Bylaw 1638 excludes "Temporary Tourist Accommodation" from Residential use except where a zone expressly permits it, and the FVRD Board specifically enabled Electoral Area H to proactively address short-term vacation rentals and RV use for accommodation. Provincially, hosts needed a registration number by May 1, 2025; electoral areas are exempt from the principal-residence rule unless the board opts in. A seller's Airbnb history is not proof a buyer can continue it.

Flood / alluvial fans: Floodplain Management Bylaw No. 1669, 2022 applies region-wide except municipalities and Park lands — so it applies here — and requires alluvial-fan development to meet the Flood Construction Level/setback set by a site-specific geohazard assessment by a Professional Engineer/Geoscientist. The FVRD's Frosst Creek works protect the community on the Frosst Creek alluvial fan at the lake's south end: two debris basins and two dikes.

Rural property tax penalty — the regime that applies here: under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, rural taxes are due and payable on July 2 of the year levied, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid on July 2 and a further 5% penalty on amounts unpaid on October 31 (s. 11). Lindell Beach properties pay provincial rural taxes plus FVRD service parcel taxes for water and sewer where connected. This staged 5% + 5% rural regime — not any city's penalty schedule — is the one that applies to this unincorporated ground.

blocks.text: Good to know about Lindell Beach townhomes

items.t: The mailing address lies about the government. "Chilliwack, BC" is a postal address only — permits, zoning enforcement, water and sewer all run through the FVRD in Electoral Area H, and a buyer who calls Chilliwack City Hall about a Lindell Beach lot will be redirected.

The two shores of the same lake run on opposite tenures. North-shore Cultus Lake Park homes sit on leased Park Board land; Lindell Beach, at the south end, is predominantly freehold — except its named resort, where you own a trailer on a leased pad. Three tenure models within one lake, and each property's title has to be read on its own.

South-shore water and sewer send no utility bill. FVRD Area H rates fund Cultus Lake water and South Cultus Lake sewer through property taxes ("No Utility Billing / Property Taxes: Yes"), and the South Cultus sewer parcel tax is split equally across every parcel on the roll — while the lake's north sewer carries a $1,369.00 flat rate for 2026. Same lake, different billing model. Area H - Residential Rates 2026.pdf

The lake's sewage system is mid-upgrade, north side first. The FVRD's North Cultus wastewater plant was commissioned in April 2025 (construction from July 2023) under the FVRD Liquid Waste Management Plan, for Class A effluent plus phosphorus removal; 2025 was its first operational year, north side only.

One road in, one road out. Columbia Valley Road is the community's only access — summer lake traffic, emergencies and winter conditions are part of the ownership picture, and there is no transit alternative: no bus serves the south shore, and Route 56 reaches only the north-end Marina, in summer.

Area H residents vote for Chilliwack school trustees. Although the FVRD governs the land, Area H elects SD33 (Chilliwack) school trustees — the school connection is the one civic tie to Chilliwack that is real.

A fresh townhouse search for this area returns detached houses. The November 2, 2026 verification search for Lindell Beach townhouse/strata product surfaced Aquadel Crossing and Creekside Mills listings — both filed by their own sources as Single Family Residence / detached houses on strata lots. A buyer who stops at the search result will think the lake has townhouse complexes; the form on the ground is bare-land strata cottages.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Lindell Beach
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple lots: the beach strip's cottages and custom lake homes are predominantly freehold — no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees; FVRD zoning plus any registered covenants govern instead. The cottage community is 60+ years old; stock ranges from original small cabins to large modern rebuilds. Tenure of any individual property must be checked on title — especially resort properties (below).

The three communities above are documented in full in the Lindell Beach condos page (which counts 0 apartment condos for this area) and carried in the townhomes page (which counts 0 townhouse-form complexes).
Pad tenure: a manufactured home on a rented pad is not lot stock and is not land ownership.

Hazard character of the land: the governing local hazards are lake-level and creek (Frosst Creek) debris/flood events on the Cultus Lake alluvial fans rather than Fraser River flooding — the FVRD's Frosst Creek works (two debris basins and two dikes, south and north sides of the creek, partly on private property) protect the community on the Frosst Creek alluvial fan at the lake's south end.

SSMUH / subdivision potential, as the jurisdiction states it: Do not carry any municipal four-unit assumption onto an Area H lot.

Short-term rentals — an FVRD zoning gate, actively enforced here: the FVRD Board specifically enabled Electoral Area H (Lindell Beach) to proactively address short-term vacation rentals and RV use for accommodation. No city penalty schedule applies to this unincorporated ground.

ALR block (applies where a parcel is in the ALR — status per-parcel): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page — on a bare-land strata lot the Form B and the strata plan are how a buyer learns what the corporation owns and maintains (roads, water/sewer infrastructure, amenities); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF since November 1, 2023; rental bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (the STR gate above is zoning, not the strata); only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). A fee-simple lot carries none of this.
Manufactured homes and pad rent (MHPTA frame): The frame governs the Holiday Resort's leased pads and park product elsewhere at the lake; it does not apply to a home on land the owner also owns.

buying a home at Cultus Lake: the rules

faq.a: Apartment condos: none — zero known. What the community calls its "condo" product is three bare-land strata / detached communities (Creekside Mills, 129 homes, EPS3777; The Cottages at Cultus Lake, 231 cottages; Aquadel Crossing, gated detached homes) where you buy a detached house on a strata lot.
faq.q: Are there condos in Lindell Beach?

faq.a: Not municipally. It is an unincorporated community in FVRD Electoral Area H with a Chilliwack mailing address; the FVRD is its local government, and its plan/zoning are FVRD documents (OCP Bylaw 1115; Zoning Bylaw 1638), not City bylaws.
faq.q: Is Lindell Beach part of Chilliwack?

faq.a: None that I know of. Creekside Mills, The Cottages and Aquadel Crossing are all general-market. The nearest known 55+ strata stock is in the City of Chilliwack.
faq.q: Is there a 55+ community in Lindell Beach I can buy into?

faq.a: No. The park behind those results is Cultus Lake Village, 3942 Columbia Valley Road, in Cultus Lake East by the golf course — not Lindell Beach — it is a pad-rental park, and its own listings disagree on the age (55+ in one, 45+ in others).
faq.q: A search showed a "55+ park" at Cultus Lake. Is that Lindell Beach?

faq.a: Not by default: Bylaw 1638 excludes Temporary Tourist Accommodation from Residential use unless the zone expressly permits it, the FVRD has specifically enabled STR enforcement in Electoral Area H, and a provincial STR registration number has been required since May 1, 2025. Long-term rental-restriction bylaws in a strata are void since November 24, 2022 — the STR gate is zoning, not the strata.
faq.q: Can I rent out a Lindell Beach cottage short-term?

faq.a: Not municipally. It is an unincorporated community in FVRD Electoral Area H with a Chilliwack mailing address; the FVRD is its local government, and its plan and zoning are FVRD documents (OCP Bylaw 1115; Zoning Bylaw 1638), not City of Chilliwack bylaws.
faq.q: Is Lindell Beach part of Chilliwack?

faq.a: No: you own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — the documented model (2009 BCCA 5) is a pre-fabricated holiday trailer on a leased pad.
faq.q: At the Holiday Resort, do I own the land?

faq.a: No — they are bare-land strata / gated single-family communities: you buy a strata lot (land) plus the home on it, under the Strata Property Act, not a pad tenancy. Their land form is documented in the cultus-lake-south lots home.
faq.q: Are Creekside Mills, the Cottages and Aquadel mobile home parks?

faq.a: Only where the zone expressly permits Temporary Tourist Accommodation under Bylaw 1638, and a provincial STR registration number has been required since May 1, 2025.
faq.q: Can I run a short-term rental?

faq.a: The exception that proves the rule is the Holiday Resort, where the documented model is an owned trailer on a leased pad — check title on every individual property.
faq.q: Is this the same tenure as Cultus Lake Park?

faq.a: Fvrd service bylaws cover Cultus Lake water supply and South Cultus Lake sewage treatment, with parcel taxes for participating properties — confirm connection status lot by lot; south-shore services are tax-funded, and the sewer parcel tax is shared equally across the roll.
faq.q: Is Lindell Beach on sewer and water, or septic and well?

faq.a: Under the rural regime (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11): July 2, with 5% penalties after July 2 and a further 5% after October 31 — not a city tax calendar.
